about.title: Redlands Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Redlands who walk out of an appointment feeling uneasy never learn whether something actually went wrong. A missed lab result, a rushed discharge, a medication that should have been checked against another — these things surface slowly, and by the time they do, the calendar has already started moving under California's MICRA rules. Injuries here come from all directions: in 2025 alone, 671 people were hurt in 477 injury collisions across the city, many along I-10, Orange Street, Alabama Street and Lugonia Avenue, and injured people need emergency care and follow-up afterward. That care is usually sound. Sometimes it isn't. LawProactive exists for the second case. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that listens to what happened to you in San Bernardino County and connects you with an independent attorney who handles medical negligence claims on contingency. Whether your case has merit is a question for that attorney and, almost always, a qualified medical expert — not for us, and not for a website.

whyChoose.title: Why Redlands Patients Start With LawProactive

items.title: MICRA's clock is shorter than most people expect
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it occurred, plus a 90-day notice to the provider before suit. An attorney can tell you quickly where you stand on those dates.

items.title: A bad result is not the same as negligence
items.desc: California law asks whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care, and proving that almost always requires a qualified medical expert. The attorneys in our network know how to evaluate that question before anyone commits to a case.

items.title: The cap on non-economic damages changes every year
items.desc: MICRA limits pain-and-suffering damages, but the limit rises annually, so the figure that applied to a neighbor's case a few years ago may not apply to yours. Your attorney will explain the current number and what it does and does not cover.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-10 near Redlands and I think the emergency room missed something. Is that a car accident case or a malpractice case?
items.answer: It may be both, and they are handled as separate claims with separate rules. The crash claim looks at the other driver; the malpractice claim looks at whether the ER fell below the standard of care and whether that failure made your injury worse. A qualified medical expert would need to support the second part. An attorney can sort out which claims exist and how their deadlines interact.

items.question: What does the 90-day notice mean, and do I have to send it myself?
items.answer: Before filing a medical malpractice lawsuit in California, the provider must receive at least 90 days' written notice of the intent to sue. It does not need to be complicated, but its timing can affect your filing deadline, so it is usually prepared by the attorney handling your case. This is one of the reasons people reach out earlier rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything, and who actually represents me?
items.answer: LawProactive is free to use and is not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles medical negligence matters in San Bernardino County. That attorney works on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and you decide whether to move forward after speaking with them.
